title: CBEVAL: A FRAMEWORK FOR EVALUATING AND INTERPRETING COGNITIVE BIASES IN LLMS

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring shifts in model preference probabilities and calculating Shapley value attributions when the same underlying information is presented with positive versus negative framing.
Introducing arbitrary numerical anchors in prompts and using Shapley value analysis to determine the influence of those specific anchor tokens on the model's final numerical prediction or evaluation.
Analyzing model output probability distributions across numerical ranges and zero-shot essay grading tasks to identify anomalous preference spikes at round numbers (e.g., multiples of 5 or 10).

Testing models on classic cognitive psychology dilemmas (such as base-rate fallacy tests and Monty Hall variations) to see if they ignore statistical likelihood in favor of matching mental prototypes.
Exposing the model to specific prior stimuli (e.g., color keywords) in the prompt and using preference scores and Shapley values to measure the unconscious influence on subsequent related decisions.
